title: Quick start
description: Make your first API request and choose the right integration path.
markdown:
## Obtain an API Key

### **Option 1: MuseDAM administration**

1. Sign in as an administrator and open MuseDAM Settings and Members.
2. Open Security Controls → API Keys.
3. Select Create New Key.

![Open API Keys and select Create New Key (Chinese interface).](/assets/developers/api-key/entry.png)

4. Name the key and choose its permission type:

   - API permissions: access assets in specified folders.
   - Admin permissions: access all assets in the library.

![Enter a name and choose API or Administrator permissions.](/assets/developers/api-key/create.png)

5. Save and copy the API Key. It is shown only once.

![After creation, open key details to check its type and status. The key is masked in this screenshot.](/assets/developers/api-key/detail.png)

> For API-scoped keys, administrators must configure the allowed folders and access restrictions under Shared Folders → Folder Permissions.

### **Option 2: Third-party application API**

[Read app authentication and installation](./applications)

> After an enterprise administrator enables and authorizes an application, it can use appId and appSecretKey to manage API Keys, then call the Open API with the issued key.

## Authentication

Include authentication in every API request:

```text
Authorization: Bearer your_api_key
Content-Type: application/json
```

## Integration recommendations

Call the API from your backend rather than directly from browser code:

- Keep API Keys out of client-side code.
- Prevent unauthorized access.
- Apply additional access controls and request limits on your server.
- Centralize API usage management and monitoring.

Your frontend should send requests to your own backend, which calls MuseDAM on its behalf.

## Make your first request

Set `MUSEDAM_API_KEY` in your server environment, then run the command below. Mainland China and overseas accounts use different API domains. This English example uses the overseas endpoint.

```bash
curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/search-assets' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $MUSEDAM_API_KEY" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"keywords": ["brand"], "startPoint": 0, "endPoint": 10}'
```

## Handle the response

Read `result.assets` and `result.total`. For empty results, check the search criteria and folder permissions. Save `traceId` from failed responses for troubleshooting.

[Asset search parameters](./search) · [Error handling](./errors)

title: Authentication
description: Authenticate requests, select your region, and manage API keys securely.
markdown:
## Security best practices

- **API Key protection**

  - Never expose API Keys in frontend code.
  - Store keys in environment variables.
  - Rotate API Keys regularly.
- **Access control**

  - Apply least-privilege access.
  - Use separate API Keys for different integrations.
  - Monitor API usage.
- **Network security**

  - Access the API over HTTPS only.

## API Key quotas and pricing

#### Included quota

- Each enterprise account includes **5 API Keys** at no additional charge.
- Keys can have API permissions (specified folders) or Admin permissions (the entire library).

#### Additional keys

- Beyond 5 keys, each additional API Key costs **CNY 3,000 per year** in the referenced policy.
- Additional keys can be purchased at any time and are billed annually.

## API rate limits (QPS)

Queries per second vary by endpoint and resource usage:

| Endpoint category | QPS |
|-|-|
| **Read operations** | |
| Batch asset retrieval | 5 |
| Asset search | 10 |
| **Write operations** | |
| Asset upload | 5 |
| Asset metadata update | 10 |
| **Management operations** | |
| Folder subscriptions | 5 |

## Handling rate limits

The source specification does not define the rate-limit response format or retry contract. Limit concurrency and use bounded backoff for retryable errors. Confirm the outcome of writes before retrying to avoid duplicates.

## Permission scope

| **Operation** | **API permissions** | **Admin permissions** |
|-|-|-|
| View folder assets | Specified folders only | All folders in the library |
| View specific assets | Specified folders only | Any asset |
| View all assets | Specified folders only | Entire library |
| Upload assets | Specified folders with upload permission | All Assets or any folder |
| Update basic metadata (name, description, source, rating) | Specified folders with edit permission | Entire library |
| Search assets | Specified folders only | Entire library |
| Subscribe to folders | Specified folders only | Any folder |

> Quotas and prices come from API v1.5 (2026-02-06). Confirm current terms and regional pricing with MuseDAM before enabling the service.

markdown:
## Search assets

**Endpoint**: /search-assets

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Search assets in an enterprise workspace.

**Request parameters**:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| - | EnterpriseSearchReqVO | Yes | Asset search parameters |

**EnterpriseSearchReqVO fields**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| parentId | Long | No | Search within this folder, excluding the root directory; includes descendants |
| needChildren | Boolean | No | Include assets in child folders; default false |
| extensions | List<String> | No | File extensions |
| color | String | No | Color |
| areaThreshold | Integer | No | Color coverage threshold; default 20 |
| colorThreshold | Integer | No | Color precision threshold; default 20 |
| minLength | Long | No | Minimum video/audio duration in ms |
| maxLength | Long | No | Maximum video/audio duration in ms |
| minSize | Long | No | Minimum file size in bytes |
| maxSize | Long | No | Maximum file size in bytes |
| minHeight | Long | No | Minimum image height in px |
| maxHeight | Long | No | Maximum image height in px |
| minWidth | Long | No | Minimum image width in px |
| maxWidth | Long | No | Maximum image width in px |
| startTime | Long | No | Start of the update-time range |
| endTime | Long | No | End of the update-time range |
| keywords | List<String> | No | Search keywords |
| tags | List<Long> | No | Tag IDs |
| tagOrAnd | Boolean | No | Combine tags with OR/AND; true means AND; default true |
| createUsers | List<Long> | No | Creator IDs |
| ratings | List<Integer> | No | Ratings (scores) |
| hasLink | Boolean | No | Whether an associated link exists |
| link | String | No | Link to match |
| hasDesc | Boolean | No | Whether a description exists |
| desc | String | No | Description to match |
| sort | SortConditionVO | No | Sort criteria |
| startPoint | Integer | No | Pagination start index; default 0 |
| endPoint | Integer | No | Pagination end index; default 10 |
| region | List<Float> | No | Search region coordinates |
| customFieldTemplateIds | List<Long> | No | Custom field template IDs |
| customFieldId | Long | No | Custom field ID |
| currentUserId | Long | No | Restrict results to assets accessible to this user |
| w | Integer | No | Target width in px, 1–6000; used to generate publicUrl; values exceeding the original image dimensions have no effect |
| h | Integer | No | Target height in px, 1–6000; used to generate publicUrl; values exceeding the original image dimensions have no effect |
| mode | String | No | publicUrl resize mode: fit (proportional) or crop (center crop); default fit |
| q | Integer | No | Output quality, 1–100; used to generate publicUrl |
| f | String | No | Output format: jpg / png / webp; used to generate publicUrl |
| bg | String | No | Background color in HEX without #; used to generate publicUrl |
| keywordSearchType | String | No | DEEP (deep search, default), DEFAULT (standard in-app search), PRECISE (exact search), or DEEP_AND_PRECISE (both) |

**SortConditionVO fields**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| sortName | SortConditionFieldEnum | Yes | Sort field |
| sortType | SortTypeEnum | No | Sort direction |

**SortConditionFieldEnum values**:

| Value | Description |
|-|-|
| CREATE_TIME | Creation time |
| UPDATE_TIME | Update time |
| NAME | Name |
| DURATION | Duration |
| SIZE | Size |
| SCORE | Rating |

**SortTypeEnum values**:

| Value | Description |
|-|-|
| ASC | Ascending |
| DESC | Descending |

**Response fields**:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| assets | List<MiniDamAssetDTO> | Assets |
| total | Long | Total count |

**MiniDamAssetDTO fields**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| id | Long | Asset ID |
| parentIds | List<Long> | Parent folder IDs |
| userId | String | User ID |
| name | String | Original filename |
| downloadUrl | String | Download URL |
| source | Integer | Asset source: 1 web, 2 upload, 3 copy |
| link | String | Webpage URL |
| extension | String | File extension |
| duration | Long | Video duration |
| size | Long | File size in KB |
| width | Integer | File width |
| height | Integer | File height |
| description | String | Description |
| score | Integer | Rating |
| createTime | Date | Creation time |
| createUser | String | Creator |
| updateTime | Date | Update time |
| updateUser | Long | Last updated by |
| tags | List<TagDTO> | Tags |
| thumbnailAccessUrl | String | Thumbnail URL |
| imageContentAnalysis | ImageContentAnalysis | AI analysis |
| publicUrl | String | Processed public link using w/h/mode/q/f/bg; empty if no processing parameters or public link are available |

### Copyright management and license validity

Assets returned by `/search-assets` and `/assets-by-ids` follow the same rules, controlled by the team's `licenseManagement` setting:

- **Copyright management enabled**: read validity dates and status from `licenseAgreements[].scopes[]`. An agreement can contain multiple scopes; check each scope's region, channel and validity separately. Do not substitute asset-level validity for agreement validity.
- **Copyright management disabled**: read the asset-level `validStartTime`, `validEndTime`, `isPermanent`, `validityStatus` and `daysToExpire`. `licenseAgreements` is null or omitted.

These are additional **response fields, not search filters**. The existing search request fields `startTime` / `endTime` filter update timestamps, not asset validity.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| licenseAgreements | List<MaterialLicenseAgreementDTO> | License agreements when copyright management is enabled |
| validStartTime | Date | Asset validity start when copyright management is disabled |
| validEndTime | Date | Asset validity end when copyright management is disabled |
| isPermanent | Boolean | Whether the asset is permanently valid when copyright management is disabled |
| validityStatus | Integer | Asset validity: 1=pending, 2=valid, 3=expiring soon, 4=expired, 5=permanent |
| daysToExpire | Integer | Days remaining until expiry, rounded up; 99999 for permanent validity, -1 when unknown |

**MaterialLicenseAgreementDTO (`licenseAgreements` item):**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| agreementId | Long | Agreement ID |
| agreementName | String | Agreement name |
| rightHolder | String | Rights holder |
| scopes | List<AgreementScopeDTO> | License scopes |

**AgreementScopeDTO (`licenseAgreements[].scopes` item):**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| authorizedRegion | String | Licensed region |
| authorizedChannel | String | Licensed channel |
| effectiveDate | Date | License validity start |
| expireDate | Date | License validity end |
| isPermanent | Integer | Whether this scope is permanently valid: 0=no, 1=yes; unlike the asset-level Boolean |
| licenseStatus | String | License status |
| licenseStatusText | String | License status display text |

> Read date fields using the API's actual serialization format. Missing or unknown validity does not imply permanent validity.

**TagDTO fields**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| id | Long | Tag ID |
| name | String | Tag name |

**ImageContentAnalysis fields**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| aiTags | String | AI-generated tags |
| aiTitle | String | AI-generated title |
| aiDescription | String | AI-generated description |
| aiDetailedDescription | JSONArray | Detailed AI analysis |

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/search-assets' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "parentId": 100,
```

markdown:
## Upload assets

**Endpoint**: /upload-assets

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Upload assets to the DAM system.

**Request parameters**:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| - | List<EnterpriseAssetSaveReq> | Yes | Asset save requests |

This section describes uploading from a downloadable URL. The parameters below apply to this integration method.

**EnterpriseAssetSaveReq fields**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| folderIds | List<Long> | No | Target folder IDs. If empty, global upload permission such as upload to all assets is required. Otherwise, upload permission is required for every folder |
| name | String | No | Display filename; if omitted, the server attempts to infer it from the `url` path |
| url | String | Yes | **Directly downloadable** asset URL (GET returns 200). The server downloads the file and stores it under a new key. Avoid short links blocked by hotlink protection or regional restrictions |
| extension | String | Yes | File extension, such as `jpg` or `mp4`, matching the resource type |
| size | Long | No | Declared size in bytes. **The stored file size takes precedence after upload**. Use the local size to assist validation |
| width | Integer | No | Image or video cover width in pixels. For **images**, the server attempts to read it from the downloaded file when omitted |
| height | Integer | No | Image or video cover height in pixels. For **images**, the server attempts to read it from the downloaded file when omitted |
| duration | Long | No | Video duration in **milliseconds** |
| link | String | No | Associated webpage or source link |
| description | String | No | Notes |
| rating | Integer | No | Rating; written to the asset rating field, corresponding to internal `score` |
| userId | Long | No | Asset owner user ID; defaults to the creator (the API key user). A specified user must belong to the current team |
| oldAssetId | Long | No | Original asset ID (>0) when **uploading a new version**; used for cover/version association |
| metadatas | List<MetadataDTO> | No | Custom metadata; **only effective when enabled for the team**. `fieldId` must match an ID from the metadata fields endpoint. Field validity is checked |
| skipDuplicateByEtag | Boolean | No | Skip duplicates. When true, the server checks the team's OSS ETags after downloading to the asset bucket but before adding to the library. Existing identical content is not added again; returned id, key, and accessUrl refer to the existing asset. Defaults to false |
| licenseAgreementIds | List<Long> | No | Linked license agreement IDs; only effective when copyright management is enabled, otherwise ignored |
| startTime | Date | No | Asset validity start; only effective when copyright management is disabled, otherwise ignored |
| endTime | Date | No | Asset validity end; only effective when copyright management is disabled, otherwise ignored |
| isPermanent | Boolean | No | Whether the asset is permanently valid; only effective when copyright management is disabled, otherwise ignored |

Upload requests use `startTime` / `endTime` to set asset validity; search and batch retrieval return `validStartTime` / `validEndTime`. With copyright management enabled, link agreements using `licenseAgreementIds`; validity comes from the agreement scopes.

**MetadataDTO (`metadatas` item):**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| fieldId | String | Conditional | Metadata field ID used **during upload**, matching the fields endpoint; paired with `value` |
| value | Object | No | Field value; type must match the field definition |

**Response fields**:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| assets | List<Item> | Successfully saved assets |

**Item fields**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| id | Long | Asset ID |
| key | String | File URL, OSS key, or downloadable file |
| storePath | String | Asset OSS storage path; same as key |
| skippedDuplicateByEtag | Boolean | true when an existing team asset is reused after an ETag match; id, key, and accessUrl refer to that asset |
| name | String | Title |
| accessUrl | String | Access URL |
| uploadResult | String | NEW: newly uploaded and added to the library. DUPLICATE_BY_ETAG: duplicate found; no new asset added |

**Example**:

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/upload-assets' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '[
    {
        "folderIds": [
            23015
        ],
        "url": "https://example.com/assets/sample.jpg",
        "name": "Sample image",
        "extension": "jpeg"
    }
]'
```

Response example:

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "assets": [
            {
                "id": 6908936,
                "key": "api_b9648d4570d2e08364a451b1eec88eea.jpeg",
                "storePath": "api_b9648d4570d2e08364a451b1eec88eea.jpeg",
                "uploadResult": "NEW",
                "skippedDuplicateByEtag": false,
                "name": "Sample image",
                "accessUrl": "https://example.com/assets/sample.jpg"
            }
        ]
    }}
```

## Download assets

Asset downloads do not require a separate endpoint. Obtain a download link in either of these ways:

1. Search assets: each asset returned by `/search-assets` includes a `downloadUrl` field.
2. Retrieve assets in bulk: the batch asset retrieval response also includes download links.

Use `downloadUrl` directly to download the asset. Links generally contain the required authentication and access information and can be opened in a browser or used with a download tool.

**Notes:**

- Download links may expire after 10 hours. Use them promptly.
- Ensure a stable connection when downloading large files.
- For batch downloads, consider server-side scripts to reduce client download failures.

## Modify assets

**Endpoint**: /modify-assets

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Update basic asset information such as name, description, and rating.

**Request parameters**:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| - | AssetModifyReq | Yes | Asset modification request |

**AssetModifyReq fields**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| id | Long | Yes | Asset ID |
| name | String | No | Filename |
| description | String | No | Description |
| score | Integer | No | Rating (1–5) |
| link | String | No | Webpage link |
| tags | List<Long> | No | Tag IDs |

**Response fields**:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| - | MiniDamAssetDTO | Updated asset information |

**MiniDamAssetDTO fields**:

[See MiniDamAssetDTO fields in asset search](./search)

**Example**:

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/modify-assets' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "id":6908914,
    "name":"bottomTip45",
    "description":"description 451",
    "score":5,
    "link":"wwww.baidu.com"
}'
```

### Move assets to a folder

**Endpoint**: `/move-assets-to-folder`

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Move or add a batch of assets from a source folder to a target folder.

**Request parameters**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| assetIds | List<Long> | Yes | Asset IDs; maximum 200 per request |
| fromFolderId | Long | Conditional | Required and >0 when operationType=0 (move). The current folder association to remove |
| toFolderId | Long | Yes | Target folder ID (>0) |
| operationType | Integer | No | 0: move (remove from fromFolderId and add to toFolderId); 1: add (keep source association). Defaults to 0 |

**Response**: Boolean

**Example request** (move):

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/move-assets-to-folder' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
  "assetIds": [6908914, 6908820],
  "fromFolderId": 10001,
  "toFolderId": 10002,
  "operationType": 0
}'
```

**Notes**:

- Assets and folders must exist and belong to the current team. Edit permission for the relevant folders is required.
- operationType=0 moves assets; =1 adds them while keeping them in both folders.

## Retrieve assets in bulk

**Endpoint**: /assets-by-ids

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Retrieve asset details for a list of asset IDs.

**Request parameters**:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| - | List<Long> | Yes | Asset IDs |

**Response fields**:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| - | List<MiniDamAssetDTO> | Asset information |

**MiniDamAssetDTO fields**:

[See MiniDamAssetDTO fields in asset search](./search)

**Example**:

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/assets-by-ids' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '[6908914,6908820]'
```

Response example:

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": [
        {
            "id": 6908914,
            "parentIds": [
                28566
            ],
            "userId": "1673603133161799680",
```

## Tag management APIs

### Merge tags in bulk

**Endpoint**: `/merge-tags`

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Merge enterprise tags in bulk, optionally clearing existing tags or merging new ones.

**Request parameters**:

```json
{
    "tags": [
        {
            "id": 10837,
            "name": "Product categories",
            "operation": 1,
            "children": [
                {
                    "id": 10838,
                    "name": "Clothing and accessories",
                    "operation": 1,
                    "sort": 4,
                    "children": [
                        {
                            "name": "add2",
                            "operation": "2"
                        }
                    ]
                },
                {
                    "id": 10839,
                    "sort": 5,
                    "operation": 1,
                    "name":"Electronics"
                }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

**Parameters**:

- `tags`: Hierarchical tag list

  - `name`: Tag name
  - `id`: Tag ID
  - `operation`: 0 no change, 1 update, 2 create, 3 delete; defaults to 0
  - `sort`: Sort value; tags are ordered from highest to lowest
  - `children`: Child tags; multiple nesting levels are supported

Notes:

```text
For operation 1, id and name are required, the tag must exist, and name must be unique among sibling tags.
For operation 2, id must be empty and name must be unique among sibling tags.
For operation 3, id is required and the tag must exist.
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {

                        "sort": 4,
                        "children": [
                            {
                                "name": "add2",
                                "id": 13945,

                                "children": null
                            }

                    {
                        "name": "Electronics",
                        "id": 10839,
                        "operation": 1,
                        "sort": 5,
                        "children": null
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    },
    "traceId": "17582767681984319367"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/merge-tags' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
```

title: Folders
description: Search folders, retrieve paths, and create folder trees.
markdown:
## Folder management

### Get folder paths

**Endpoint**: `/folder-path`

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Get complete paths for specified folders.

**Request parameters**:

```json
[123, 456, 789]
```

**Parameters**:

- A list of folder IDs.

**Response**:

```json
{
  "code": "200",
  "message": "OK",
  "result": {
    "123": "Root/Child folder 1/Child folder 2",
    "456": "Root/Other folder",
    "789": "Root/Sample folder"
  }
}
```

**Behavior**:

- Builds the full path from the folder treeCode.
- Returns a map of folder IDs to path strings.
- Uses / as the path separator.

---

### Get descendant folder IDs

**Endpoint**: `/get-sub-folder-ids`

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Get all descendant folder IDs for specified folders.

**Request parameters**:

```json
[123, 456, 789]
```

**Parameters**:

- A list of parent folder IDs.

**Response**:

```json
{
  "code": "200",
  "message": "OK",
  "result": {
    "123": [123,124, 125, 126],
    "456": [456,457, 458],
    "789": [789]
  }
}
```

**Behavior**:

- Recursively queries all descendant levels.
- Returns a map of parent folder IDs to folder ID lists.
- Supports querying multiple parent folders in one request.

---

### Get folder auto-tags

**Endpoint**: `/folder-auto-tags`

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Batch-query auto-tags configured directly on folders, excluding tags inherited from ancestor folders.

**Request parameters**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| folderIds | List<Long> | Yes | Up to 50 existing folder IDs in the current organization |

**Response**: Map<Long, List>, keyed by folderId. Folders with no auto-tags return an empty array.

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| id | Long | Tag ID |
| name | String | Tag name |
| parentId | Long | Parent tag ID |
| parent | Object | Recursive parent tag; null when absent |

**Request example**:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/folder-auto-tags' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "folderIds": [10001, 10002]
}'
```

## Search folders

**Endpoint:** `/search-folders`

**Method:** POST

**Request parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description | Default |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| parentId | Long | No | Folder scope, including descendants; omit to search all folders; 0 means root | - |
| needChildren | Boolean | No | With parentId set, true searches that folder and all descendants; false searches direct children only | false |
| keywords | List<String> | No | Multiple search keywords; ignored when parentId=0 | - |
| sort | Object | No | Sort criteria | - |
| sort.sortName | String | Yes, if sort is provided | CREATE_TIME, UPDATE_TIME, NAME, SIZE or SCORE | - |
| sort.sortType | String | No | ASC (ascending) or DESC (descending) | DESC |
| startPoint | Integer | No | Pagination start index | 0 |
| endPoint | Integer | No | Pagination end index | 10 |
| currentUserId | Long | No | Search folders accessible to this user |
| folderIds | List<Long> | No | Retrieve specified folder IDs. When provided, uses direct ID lookup instead of the regular keyword and pagination search |

Request example:

```json
{
    "parentId": 1234567890,
    "needChildren": false,
    "keywords": ["sample"],
    "sort": {
        "sortName": "CREATE_TIME",
        "sortType": "DESC"
    },
    "startPoint": 0,
    "endPoint": 10
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/search-folders' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "parentId": 1234567890,
    "needChildren": false,
    "keywords": ["sample"],
    "sort": {
        "sortName": "CREATE_TIME",
        "sortType": "DESC"
    },
    "startPoint": 0,
    "endPoint": 10
}'
```

Response:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| code | String | Business status code; "0" indicates success |
| message | String | Response message |
| result | Object | Result object |
| result.folders | Array | Folder list |
| result.folders[].id | Long | Folder ID |
| result.folders[].name | String | Folder name |
| result.folders[].createUser | Long | Creator userId |
| result.folders[].userId | Long | Owner userId |
| result.total | Long | Total matching folders |
| traceId | String | Trace ID |

Example response:

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "folders": [
            {
                "id": 1234567890,
                "name": "Sample folder",
                "createUser": 1765276754630496256,
                "userId": 1765276754630496256
            },
            {
                "id": 1234567891,
                "name": "Another folder",
                "createUser": 1765276754630496257,
                "userId": 1765276754630496257
            }
        ],
        "total": 2
    },
    "traceId": "17561978534182325498"
}
```

## Create a folder

**Endpoint:** `/create-folder`

**Method:** POST

**Request parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| name | String | Yes | Folder name; cannot be empty |
| parentFolderId | Long | Yes | Parent folder ID, greater than 0. The new folder is created inside this folder |

Request example:

```json
{
    "name": "New folder",
    "parentFolderId": 1234567890
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/create-folder' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "name": "New folder",
    "parentFolderId": 1234567890
}'
```

Response:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| code | String | Business status code; "0" indicates success |
| message | String | Response message |
| result | Object | Result object |
| result.folderId | Long | ID of the created folder |
| traceId | String | Trace ID |

Example response:

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "folderId": 1234567891
    },
    "traceId": "17561978534182325498"
}
```

Notes:

- The parent folder must exist; otherwise, an error is returned.
- The creator defaults to the current team owner's user ID.
- The folder defaults to team collaboration status.

### Create a folder tree

**Endpoint**: `/create-folder-tree`

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Create an entire subtree under a parent folder in one request. Duplicate sibling names are automatically renamed to name (2), name (3), and so on. The creator defaults to the team owner; collaborators are inherited from the parent folder.

**Request parameters**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| parentFolderId | Long | Yes | Parent folder ID; >0 creates under that folder, while 0 uses the team root |
| nodes | List<Node> | Yes | Root nodes of the subtree to create |

**Node**：

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| name | String | Yes | Folder name |
| children | List<Node> | No | Child folders; nesting is supported |

**Response**:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| parentFolderId | Long | Parent folder ID |
| createdCount | Integer | Number of folders created |
| pathToFolderId | Map<String, Long> | Relative path → folder ID. Paths use the original requested names, excluding the parent directory, even if duplicate names are changed during creation |

**Request example**:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/create-folder-tree' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
  "parentFolderId": 123,
  "nodes": [
    {
      "name": "Project assets",
      "children": [
        { "name": "Product images", "children": [] },
        { "name": "Posters", "children": [] }
      ]
    }
  ]
}'
```

## Get processed public links for original assets

**Prerequisite:** DAT must be enabled.

**Endpoint:** `/processed-public-links`

**Method:** POST

**Request parameters:** `publicLinkProcessReq`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| assetIds | List<Long> | Yes | Asset IDs (assetId) |
| w | Integer | No | Target width in pixels, 1–6000; values exceeding the original width have no effect |
| h | Integer | No | Target height in pixels, 1–6000; values exceeding the original height have no effect |
| mode | String | No | Resize mode; defaults to fit. fit: preserve aspect ratio; crop: center crop |
| q | Integer | No | Output quality, 1–100; defaults to 80 |
| f | String | No | Output format: jpg / png / webp; omit to retain the original format |
| bg | String | No | Background fill color in HEX without #, such as FFFFFF |

**mode values:**

| Value | Description |
|-|-|
| fit | Scale by the longer edge, preserving aspect ratio and the full image |
| crop | Center crop to the target dimensions |

**Response:** `Map<Long, String>`

- Key：assetId  
- Value: The processed public URL for the original asset, or `""` if no public link exists or the asset is missing.

- **Key:** An asset ID from the request
- **Value:** All derivative versions under **enabled** rules; `[]` if none exist or the asset is missing

**`EnterpriseAssetDerivativeVersionDTO` fields:**

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| size | Long | File size in bytes |
| width | Integer | File width in pixels |
| height | Integer | File height in pixels |
| accessUrl | String | Download URL; populated only when `generateStatus = 1` (success) |
| publicUrl | String | Derivative public URL; available when public links are enabled for the rule and the link has been generated |
| internalName | String | Internal derivative rule name |
| displayName | String | Derivative rule display name |
| generateStatus | Integer | Generation status; see below |
| name | String | Asset name |

**generateStatus values:**

| Value | Description |
|-|-|
| 0 | Processing |
| 1 | Success |
| 2 | Failed |
| 3 | Queued |

**Example request:**

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/asset-derivative-versions' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "assetIds": [1234567890, 9876543210]
}'
```

**Example response:**

```json
{
```

### Query team members

## Send an in-app notification

**Endpoint:** `/add-in-app-notify`  

**Method:** `POST`

**Description:** Send an **in-app notification** to a user in an enterprise workspace. The notification is stored and processed through the same follow-up flow as the console, including Feishu delivery where configured. Notifications can reference folders, assets, or asset groups and cover collaboration, deletion, permission requests and decisions, comments, and team changes. Use `notificationType` together with resource fields to describe the event. This endpoint lets third-party systems send notifications in automated workflows.

**Request body:** `req`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| notificationType | String | Yes | **Must exactly match** a material service `notificationType` **code** listed below |
| receiverId | Long | Yes | Recipient user ID |
| senderId | Long | No | Sender user ID; defaults to the current user in the API context |
| resourceType | Integer | No | **Must match** a `resourceType` listed below; omit if no resource is associated |
| resourceName | String | No | Resource display name |
| content | String | No | Notification body |
| resourceId | Long | No | Associated resource ID |
| permissionApprovedRoleId | Integer | No | Requested role ID for permission request notifications |

**notificationType**

| Code | Description |
|-|-|
| collaboration | Collaboration |
| deletion | Deletion |
| permission_approved | Permission request |
| permission_success | Permission granted |
| permission_refuse | Permission denied |
| comment | Comment |
| comment_reply | Comment reply |
| share_comment | Share comment |
| share_comment_reply | Share comment reply |
| team_member_join | New member joined the team |
| team_member_quit | Member left the team |
| team_member_leave | Feishu member resigned |
| asset_upload | Asset uploaded |
| subfolder_asset_upload | Asset uploaded in a subfolder |
| asset_version_upload | Asset version uploaded |
| subfolder_asset_version_upload | Asset version uploaded in a subfolder |
| asset_version_change | Asset version changed |
| subfolder_asset_version_change | Asset version changed in a subfolder |
| asset_version_remove | Asset version removed |
| subfolder_asset_version_remove | Asset version removed in a subfolder |
| asset_version_delete | Asset version deleted |
| subfolder_asset_version_delete | Asset version deleted in a subfolder |
| folder_and_material_delete | Folder and assets deleted |
| subfolder_and_material_delete | Subfolder and assets deleted |
| folder_delete | Folder deleted |
| subfolder_delete | Subfolder deleted |
| folder_material_delete | Assets in a folder deleted |
| subfolder_material_delete | Assets in a subfolder deleted |
| folder_material_move | Assets in a folder moved |
| subfolder_material_move | Assets in a subfolder moved |
| approval | Approval |

**resourceType**

| resourceType | Description |
|-|-|
| 1 | Folder (FOLDER) |
| 2 | Asset (MATERIAL) |
| 3 | Asset group (MATERIAL_GROUP) |
| 4 | Team (TEAM) |

Use with `resourceId`, which identifies the business record of the selected type, such as a folder, asset, or team ID.

**Response:** `result` is a `Boolean`.

**Example request:**

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/add-in-app-notify' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "notificationType": "permission_approved",
    "receiverId": 1765276754630496256,
    "resourceType": 1,
    "resourceId": 1234567890,
    "resourceName": "Brand asset library",
    "content": "Request permission to view this shared folder",
    "permissionApprovedRoleId": 2
}'
```

**Example response:**

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": true,
    "traceId": "17561978534182325498"
}
```

description: Subscribe to folder events and send in-app notifications.
markdown:
## Subscribe to folders

**Endpoint**: /folder-subscribe

**Method**: POST

**Description**: Subscribe to or unsubscribe from folder content updates.

**Request parameters**:

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| - | OpenApiSubReq | Yes | Subscription parameters |

**OpenApiSubReq fields**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| folderIds | List<Long> | Yes | Folder IDs to subscribe to |
| callbackUrl | String | Yes | Callback URL |
| eventType | String | No | Callback event type; default FOLDER_CONTENT_UPDATE |
| operation | String | No | ADD to subscribe, DELETE to unsubscribe; default ADD |

**Response fields**:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| - | Boolean | Whether the operation succeeded |

**Example**:

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/folder-subscribe' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
  "folderIds": [100, 101, 102],
  "callbackUrl": "https://example.com/api/callback",
  "eventType": "FOLDER_CONTENT_UPDATE",
  "operation": "ADD"
}'
```

Response example:

```json
{
    "code": "0",
    "message": "OK",
    "result": true,
    "traceId": "1753698709474457484"
}
```

### Callback events

When a subscribed folder changes, the service sends a POST request to the callback URL with the following fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Description | Notes / example |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| eventType | String | Yes | Folder content change event identifier | Default: `FOLDER_CONTENT_UPDATE` |
| folderId | Long | Yes | Changed folder ID | e.g. `123456789` |
| eventTime | String | Yes | Event time | ISO8601 recommended: `2026-03-05T12:34:56+08:00` |
| type | String | Yes | Change type | ADD, UPDATE or DELETE |
| assets | List<MaterialCallbackDTO> | Yes | Assets affected by the change | DELETE may contain only identifiers; other events should include full details |
| orgId | Long | No | Organization ID identifying the event source | e.g. `10001`; may be optional when inferable from context |

**MaterialCallbackDTO fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Description | Notes / example |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| id | Long | Yes | Asset ID | e.g. `987654321` |
| parentIds | List<Long> | Yes | Parent folder path, from root to current parent | e.g. `[1, 23, 456]` |
| userId | String | Yes | User who triggered the change | e.g. `"10001"` |
| name | String | Yes | Original filename | e.g. `"brand-poster_v1.psd"` |
| downloadUrl | String | Yes | Authorized direct or temporary download URL | e.g. `https://example.com/download/xxx` |
| source | Integer | Yes | Asset source | 1 web, 2 upload, 3 copy |
| link | String | No | Related source webpage or external URL | e.g. a landing page or original webpage |
| extension | String | Yes | Extension without a leading dot | e.g. jpg, mp4, psd |
| duration | Long | No | Video/audio duration in seconds | 120 means 120 seconds; other files may return null or 0 |
| size | Long | Yes | File size in KB | 2048 is approximately 2 MB |
| width | Integer | No | Media width in pixels | e.g. 1920; may be null for other file types |
| height | Integer | No | Media height in pixels | e.g. 1080; may be null for other file types |
| description | String | No | Asset description or notes | e.g. Spring 2026 campaign visual |
| score | Integer | No | Asset rating | Usually 1–5; confirm the agreed range |
| createUser | String | No | Original creator, which may differ from the event initiator | Original uploader user ID |

Callback example:

```json
{
  "eventType": "FOLDER_CONTENT_UPDATE",
  "folderId": 23102,
  "eventTime": "1753946835010",
  "type": "UPDATE",
  "assets": [
    {
      "id": 6906970,
      "parentIds": [],
      "userId": "1673603133161799680",
      "name": "Ocean predators: dolphins chasing fish",
      "downloadUrl": null,
      "source": 2,
      "link": null,
      "extension": "rm",
      "duration": null,
      "size": null,
      "width": null,
      "height": null,
      "description": "11",
      "score": null,
      "createUser": "1673603133161799680"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Subscribe to asset events

**Note**: This is separate from folder subscriptions (folder-subscribe / FOLDER_CONTENT_UPDATE). Subscribe at organization level; events are delivered asynchronously via POST to callbackUrl. Notifications do not block or modify asset ingestion.

### List available event types

**Endpoint**: `/material-automation-event-types`

**Method**: GET

**Description**: Return available event types and whether the current API Key subscribes to each type.

**Response**: A list with these fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| code | String | Event code to use in eventTypes |
| desc | String | Description in Chinese |
| needsConfig | Boolean | Whether config is required; false for currently available events |
| subscribed | Boolean | Whether this API Key has an active subscription |

**Request example**:

```bash
curl --location --request GET 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/material-automation-event-types' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key'
```

### Subscribe or unsubscribe

**Endpoint**: `/material-automation-subscribe`

**Method**: POST

**Request parameters**:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-|-|-|-|
| callbackUrl | String | Yes | Webhook callback URL |
| eventTypes | List<String> | Yes | Event types from the table below; multiple types supported |
| operation | String | No | ADD to subscribe (default), DELETE to unsubscribe |

**Available eventTypes**:

| eventType | Description |
|-|-|
| MATERIAL_INBOUND_COMPLETED | Sent after successful asset ingestion; does not intercept ingestion |
| MATERIAL_ADDED_TO_FOLDER | Assets added to folders through uploads or in-app/API actions; existing relationships do not trigger duplicate notifications |
| MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED | Name, description, tags, owner or custom metadata changed |
| MATERIAL_VERSION_CHANGED | Versions added, set as cover or removed |
| MATERIAL_DELETED | Assets moved to the recycle bin or permanently deleted |

**Response**: Boolean

**Request example** (subscribe):

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse/material-automation-subscribe' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "callbackUrl": "https://your.app/webhook/material-events",
    "eventTypes": [
        "MATERIAL_INBOUND_COMPLETED",
        "MATERIAL_ADDED_TO_FOLDER",
        "MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED",
        "MATERIAL_VERSION_CHANGED",
        "MATERIAL_DELETED"
    ],
    "operation": "ADD"
}'
```

**Unsubscribe**: Set operation to DELETE. Subscriptions are identified by the current API Key, callbackUrl and eventType; no subscriptionId is required.

**Webhook callback**: The service sends a POST request to callbackUrl with this body:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-|-|-|
| eventId | String | Idempotency event ID |
| eventType | String | Event type from the table above |
| eventTime | String | Timestamp in milliseconds, encoded as a string |
| payload | Object | Event-specific payload; see below |

**Payload by event type**:

| eventType | Payload fields |
|-|-|
| MATERIAL_INBOUND_COMPLETED | source (UPLOAD_ASSETS / PENDING_INBOUND_CONFIRM), initiatorUserId. Completed uploads: uploadResults, materialIds. Confirmed pending ingestion: pendingInboundIdToMaterialId |
| MATERIAL_ADDED_TO_FOLDER | materialIds: cover asset IDs for newly created relationships; folderIds: destination folders |
| MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED | changeType (BASIC / VALIDITY / TAGS / OWNER / METADATA / CUSTOM_FIELD), materialIds, materials[] containing only changed fields for this type; see below |
| MATERIAL_VERSION_CHANGED | coverMaterialId, newMaterialId, action (ADD / SET_COVER / REPLACE_COVER_ON_UPLOAD / REMOVE); optional version. For REMOVE, coverMaterialId is the removed asset and newMaterialId is the latest asset remaining in that version chain. Optional removeType (ADD: move into the current folder; DELETE: move to recycle bin) and versionGroupDissolved |
| MATERIAL_DELETED | materialIds; deleteAction (RECYCLE / PERMANENT); optional top-level folderIds for folders deleted in the same batch; materials[] snapshots before deletion (name / materialType / extension / tagIds / tagNames / folderIds / ownerUserId / createUserId) |

**MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED materials[] by changeType**:

| changeType | Fields in each materials entry (included when populated) |
|-|-|
| BASIC | materialId; name / description / score / link supplied in this update |
| VALIDITY | materialId；validityStatus；validityStatusName；daysToExpire；startTime；endTime；isPermanent |
| TAGS | materialId；tagIds；tagNames |
| OWNER | materialId (new asset ID after transfer); ownerUserId |
| METADATA | materialId; optional recordId; metadata containing only custom fields created or updated in this operation |
| CUSTOM_FIELD | materialId；customFields：[{ "templateId": ... }] |

**Callback examples**: Each example is a complete POST body. Missing fields indicate unavailable values; allow optional fields rather than enforcing a fixed set of required properties.

**MATERIAL_INBOUND_COMPLETED** (upload successfully ingested):

```json
{
  "eventId": "evt_1753946835010_a1b2",
  "eventType": "MATERIAL_INBOUND_COMPLETED",
  "eventTime": "1753946835010",
  "payload": {
    "source": "UPLOAD_ASSETS",
    "initiatorUserId": 10001,
    "materialIds": [20001, 20002],
    "uploadResults": [
      {
        "id": 20001,
        "name": "spring-campaign.jpg",
        "extension": "jpg",
        "size": 204800,
        "width": 1920,
        "height": 1080,
        "uploadStatus": 1
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**MATERIAL_ADDED_TO_FOLDER**：

```json
{
  "eventId": "evt_1753946900001_c3d4",
  "eventType": "MATERIAL_ADDED_TO_FOLDER",
  "eventTime": "1753946900001",
  "payload": {
    "materialIds": [20001, 20002],
    "folderIds": [30001]
  }
}
```

**MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED** (changeType = BASIC; name, description and rating):

```json
{
  "eventId": "evt_1753947000002_e5f6",
  "eventType": "MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED",
  "eventTime": "1753947000002",
  "payload": {
    "changeType": "BASIC",
    "materialIds": [20001],
    "materials": [
      {
        "materialId": 20001,
        "name": "spring-campaign_v2.jpg",
        "description": "Spring 2026 key visual",
        "score": 5
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED** (changeType = TAGS):

```json
{
  "eventId": "evt_1753947050003_g7h8",
  "eventType": "MATERIAL_METADATA_UPDATED",
  "eventTime": "1753947050003",
  "payload": {
    "changeType": "TAGS",
    "materialIds": [20001],
    "materials": [
      {
        "materialId": 20001,
        "tagIds": [10837, 10838],
        "tagNames": ["Product category", "Clothing and footwear"]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**MATERIAL_VERSION_CHANGED** (new version):

## Common errors and remedies

### API authentication errors

| Error code | Description | Remedy |
|-|-|-|
| MB100002 | Access to this resource is denied | Verify the API key and its permissions for the resource |
| 401 | Unauthorized | The API key is invalid or expired. Update the key |

### Request parameter errors

| Error code | Description | Remedy |
|-|-|-|
| MB100001 | Invalid request parameters | Check parameter formats and types against the API requirements |
| MB100003 | Resource not found | Check whether the resource ID exists or has been deleted |

### Business logic errors

| Error code | Description | Remedy |
|-|-|-|
| MB100004 | Operation unsupported for this resource | Check whether the operation applies to this resource type |
| MB100005 | Business operation failed | Adjust your logic based on the error message or retry |

### System errors

| Error code | Description | Remedy |
|-|-|-|
| MS100001 | System error | Retry later. Contact support if the error persists |
| MS100003 | System busy | Rate-limit requests and retry after a delay |

## Troubleshooting sequence

1. Check the HTTP status, business `code`, and `message`. Save the `traceId`.
2. Verify the hostname, HTTP method, request body type, and key permissions.
3. Check that the resource belongs to the current organization and the required product capability is enabled.
4. Use bounded retries for temporary system failures. Fix parameter or permission errors before retrying.

Original examples use success codes such as `0`, `"0"`, and `"200"`. Confirm the success condition for each endpoint; HTTP 200 alone does not guarantee business success.

## Quick start All 31 Product Library operations use POST `https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api`. Set `service` to the operation identifier shown below and put all business parameters in a flat JSON body. 1. Obtain a MuseDAM API Key. 2. Ask a Product Library manager to add the key as an API Key Collaborator in **Member settings → Add member** and assign the required role. 3. Call the API from your server with an `Authorization: Bearer ` header. Authorization uses the key’s team and the collaborator’s current role. Request parameters cannot switch product libraries. New collaborators have the `view_only` role by default. Choose a role for the operations you need: | Role | Available operations | | --- | --- | | `view_only` | View published products. | | `usable` | View, share and download published products. | | `editable` | Create and edit products, access drafts, publish and delete products. | | `manage` | Manage all resources, including brands, categories, information templates and activity records. | Each role includes the preceding role’s permissions. Replace resource IDs in the examples with actual IDs. Replace `your_api_key` with your authorized API Key to query the product list: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "service": "listProducts", "page": 1, "pageSize": 20 }' ``` A successful response has `success: true`, a product list in `data`, and paging information in `pagination`. If the list is empty, check whether the library contains products visible to your role; `view_only` and `usable` can only view published products. ## Requests and responses Every request uses your own MuseDAM API Key in `Authorization: Bearer ` and `Content-Type: application/json`. All operations use the same public POST URL. Resource IDs, pagination, filters and write fields are JSON body fields, alongside the required `service`. JSON endpoints use the following structure. Successful downloads and exports return files directly. | Result | How to read it | | --- | --- | | Success | `success: true`; read the result from `data`. `code` and `message` are `null`. | | Failure | `success: false` and `data: null`. Handle the HTTP status and `code`; do not depend on the wording of `message`. | | Validation failure | If the response includes `details`, use `details[].field` and `details[].message` to correct the fields. | | Request tracing | Keep `requestId` or the `X-Request-Id` response header for troubleshooting. | Ordinary lists accept `page` and `pageSize` and return a top-level `pagination` object. `totalCount` is the total record count; `totalPages` is the total page count: | Parameter | Default | Range | | --- | --- | --- | | `page` | `1` | Integer starting at `1`. | | `pageSize` | `20` | Positive integer; values above `100` are capped at `100`. | ```json { "page": 1, "pageSize": 20, "totalCount": 42, "totalPages": 3 } ``` Products and assets can become invisible during a request. A page may therefore contain fewer than `pageSize` records while retaining its original counts. Reading an invisible individual resource returns `404`. Use [cursor synchronization](#cycle-protocol) to maintain a product copy; ordinary page numbers are for browsing. See each endpoint for filters. Ordinary read services ignore unknown business fields; write services reject unknown business fields. History and synchronization reads use stricter validation.
Field formats | Field | Usage | | --- | --- | | Numeric resource IDs | Positive integers up to `2147483647`. | | Template, group, field and version IDs | Strings; preserve them as received and do not assume UUID format. | | Asset IDs | Use `id` from asset lookup (FilePath ID), not an AssetObject ID or product association ID. | | Category `iconAssetId` | A category icon identifier (CategoryIconAsset). | | `size` | Decimal string or `null`, preserving large byte counts. | | Dates | RFC 3339 strings or `null`; preserve all six fractional digits in synchronization timestamps. | | Product SKU | The API field is named `spu`. | Legacy or unresolved product media can have `id: null`. Valid media references are not truncated. See [Media links](#media-and-expiry) for previews and downloads.
Concurrent updates Save the strong `ETag` (including quotes) when reading a brand, category, template, or product. Supply it as `If-Match` for an update, status change, or deletion. On `412 precondition_failed`, read and reconcile again. If omitted, the later write takes precedence. Shares, history, and download records do not use ETag.
Creation and download retries Resource creation accepts `Idempotency-Key`, scoped to the team, API key, and operation. Keys allow up to 255 characters and cannot be blank or contain control characters. Retry with the same key and input within 24 hours; changed input returns `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Resource creation replays the initial non-media result and rebuilds media using current permissions. Download retries reuse the record but authorize and transfer current files again.
Request limits and errors Request bodies are limited to 1 MiB. Write services reject unknown business fields. Ordinary read services ignore unknown business fields; history and synchronization read services validate them strictly. These rules depend on the service, not the HTTP method. | Result | Action | | --- | --- | | 401 / 403 | Check the key, collaborator role, and resource visibility. | | 404 | The resource is missing, deleted, or inaccessible; check its ID. | | 422 `validation_failed` | Correct the input. If `details` is present, read `field` and `message`. | | 409 `sku_in_use` / `name_in_use` | Change the conflicting SKU or name. Soft-deleted products still reserve their SKU. | | 409 `mutation_response_unavailable` | The mutation committed or replayed. Check `mutationOutcome`; do not blindly create again. | | 503 `write_conflict` | The mutation rolled back. Wait according to `Retry-After: 1`, then retry. | | 413 | Reduce the body or download count/size. | Use `X-Request-Id` or the JSON `requestId` for troubleshooting. A download error with `mutationOutcome` means the record committed; retain the original idempotency key when retrying.

## Products
Pinned templates and custom fields Products save a template version at creation. Interpret `templateFields` using `templateDefinition`; later template edits or deletion do not change that version. `updateProduct` cannot change the template. `templateFields` uses pinned field IDs as keys and shallow-merges on update; `null` clears an individual value. An explicit `templateId` takes priority. Otherwise a supplied `categoryId` resolves the category, ancestors, brand, then library default. Without a category, only the library default is considered, even when a brand is supplied. | Field type | Input format | | --- | --- | | `number`, `currency` | JSON number | | `dateRange` | Ordered pair of date strings | | `checkbox` | Array of option values | | `image`, `file` | Array of FilePath IDs, or null | | `richtext` | String in HTML mode; `{ "ops": [...] }` in delta mode | Drafts may omit required values, but supplied and merged fields must meet type and option rules. Publishing or editing a published product validates the complete product. A write may reference at most 100 media items across all fields, using existing same-library FilePath IDs. Omitted media lists stay unchanged; `[]` clears them. Without `coverAssetId`, the first `imageAssetIds` image becomes the cover.
Synchronization and checkpoints 1. Start with `"sync": "true"`, omitting `updatedAfter` for a full scan. For an incremental cycle, use the previous completed `syncedUntil`. 2. Merge by product `id` and `updatedAt`, retaining the newer version. 3. Follow `nextCursor` with `"sync": "true", "cursor": ""` until null, including when `data` is empty. 4. Save the completed `syncedUntil` unchanged, not the last product timestamp. Cursors bind the key, role, library, filters, and page size; keep them unchanged while paging. Start a new cycle after authorization or filter changes, and scan fully when the scope expands. Preserve all six fractional digits in checkpoints and sync `updatedAt`; JavaScript Date loses precision. Each cycle reads current state in `[updatedAfter, syncedUntil)`, with the first request’s server time minus 30 seconds as its upper bound. Longer transactions may still affect completeness; this is not an event stream of every change.
Removing deleted or invisible products Sync does not return deletion events. Periodically send local product IDs to [visibility checking](#operation-checkProductVisibility), removing local copies marked `not_visible`. Visibility does not check business filters such as brand, category, or search. For a filtered replica, periodically reconcile the full filtered result or sync all visible products and filter locally.
Preview and download links Use `previewUrl` to display product media. For originals, check `downloadUrl` or use the download operations below; preview access does not establish download permission. | Link | Availability | Maximum service-issued lifetime | | --- | --- | --- | | Derived preview | Appropriate viewing permission | 3600 seconds | | Original-image preview fallback | Images only; may also be returned to `view_only` | 300 seconds | | `downloadUrl` | Resolvable, visible association; `usable` or higher plus `products:read` and `products:download` | 300 seconds | Every service-issued link is also bounded by the API key's expiry. Fetch product data again after a link expires; do not persist signed URLs as asset identifiers.
Which fields do covers, images, and related assets return? `cover` is one media object, or null when there is no cover. `images` and `relatedAssets` are arrays of media objects. Custom image/file values may be arrays or null; unset fields may be omitted. | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `id` | Integer or null | ID returned by asset lookup (FilePath ID), not an AssetObject ID or product-asset association ID | | `name`, `mimeType` | String or null | File name and MIME type | | `size` | String or null | Decimal byte count, such as `"2048"`; never a JSON number | | `width`, `height`, `duration` | Number or null | Media dimensions and duration | | `previewUrl` | URL or null | Preview for display; null when unavailable | | `downloadUrl` | URL or null; may be omitted | Original file URL; availability is described above | | `downloadUrlExpiresAt` | Timestamp or null; may be omitted | Download URL expiry in RFC 3339 format |
How do missing links, legacy media, and external previews behave? - Non-image assets only return derived previews. Original PDFs, archives, and documents never serve as preview fallbacks. Library asset lookup and template configuration contain previews only. - Missing download permission or an unresolved association omits `downloadUrl` and `downloadUrlExpiresAt`. With permission but an unavailable original, those values may be null. - Stored external DAM thumbnails or previews are returned only to API keys without expiry, after excluding known original URLs. The provider controls their lifetime; short expiry and provider-signature validation are not guaranteed. - For an API key with `expiresAt`, an external preview whose expiry cannot be verified is null. Signature-like query parameters are not a trusted expiry source. - Service-issued URLs keep the limits above. Signing failure never falls back to a raw storage URL.

Each ID is a positive integer up to 2147483647. | | expiresInDays | Integer | Yes | May be null; Allowed values: 7, 30, 90, null | | accessCode | String | No | Must match `^[0-9]{4}$` | | allowDownload | Boolean | Yes | — | **Response fields**: `201`; `data`: ProductShare. File selection, exports, and records List product download candidates first. Put the returned `key` in `assetKeys`, or put the raw key in the single-file body field `assetKey`; it is not a FilePath ID. One original returns that file; multiple originals return a ZIP. A request selects 1–100 products, at most 200 files, and no more than 500 MiB. Exports use `kind: "export"`, with xlsx (default), csv, or json. Do not send `assetKeys`. `includeAssetUrls` defaults to true; exported links still require a Bearer header. Create a share for visitors without credentials. `locale` affects system labels and status only. `X-Download-Record-Id` identifies the business record. `requested` means accepted, not transferred or saved locally. History includes browser and other API key operations across the team. Ordinary reads, previews, and direct access to storage download URLs do not create history records.

May be null | | actorName | String | Actor name. | | shareId | String | Share ID. May be null | | products | List<ProductLabelSnapshot> | Product snapshots. Optional productId returns complete matching operations; omission selects all team records. Only service, productId, page and pageSize are accepted; unknown fields return 422. The current API key or creator never implicitly narrows the list. Requires manage plus products:history, without products:read. Required role: manage. **Request parameters**: The business fields below are siblings of `service` in the JSON body. Do not wrap them in `params` or `data`. `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key` remain HTTP control headers, not business fields. | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | service | String | Yes | Service identifier; must be `listProductDownloads`. | | productId | Integer | No | Body field. Positive integer ID, up to 2147483647. | | page | Integer | No | Positive page number, default 1. | | pageSize | Integer | No | Positive page size, default 20, capped at 100. | **Response fields**: `200`; `data`: List<ProductDownloadRecord>. Required role: usable, editable or manage. **Request parameters**: The business fields below are siblings of `service` in the JSON body. Do not wrap them in `params` or `data`. `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key` remain HTTP control headers, not business fields. | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | service | String | Yes | Service identifier; must be `downloadProducts`. | | Idempotency-Key | String | No | Optional header. Unknown fields are rejected. | Field | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | kind | String | Yes | Allowed values: assets, export | | productIds | List<Integer> | Yes | Minimum items 1; Maximum items 100. Response headers: `Content-Disposition`, `X-Download-Record-Id`, `X-Idempotency-Replayed` Request example: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "service": "downloadProducts", "kind": "export", "productIds": [ 40 ], "format": "xlsx", "includeAssetUrls": true, "locale": "zh-CN" }' \ --output products.xlsx ```
Response example ```http HTTP/1.1 200 OK Content-Type: application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet Content-Disposition: attachment X-Download-Record-Id: ``` The response body contains the file bytes.
### List product download candidates **Endpoint**: https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api **Method**: POST **Description**: Returns current candidate selection keys and downloadable availability under read and download authorization. No business download record is created, and no original or preview URLs are returned. Use `downloadProductAsset` or `downloadProducts` to retrieve bytes. Required role: usable, editable or manage. **Request parameters**: The business fields below are siblings of `service` in the JSON body. Positive signed 32-bit resource ID. Positive integer ID, maximum 2147483647. | **Response fields**: `200`; `data`: List<ProductDownloadCandidate>. [field details](#fields-ProductDownloadCandidate) Request example: ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "service": "listProductDownloadAssets", "id": 40 }' ```

### Download one product original **Endpoint**: https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api **Method**: POST **Description**: Fetches one current product original identified by a raw candidate key in the JSON body. Optional 24-hour idempotency is scoped separately from `downloadProducts`, reuses the record, and still reauthorizes and transfers current bytes. Required role: usable, editable or manage. **Request parameters**: The business fields below are siblings of `service` in the JSON body. Do not wrap them in `params` or `data`. `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key` remain HTTP control headers, not business fields. | Parameter | Type | Required | Description | | - | - | - | - | | service | String | Yes | Service identifier; must be `downloadProductAsset`. | | id | Integer | Yes | Body field. Positive signed 32-bit resource ID. Positive integer ID, maximum 2147483647. | | assetKey | String | Yes | Body field. Raw selection key returned by the product download-candidate list; do not URL-encode it. Not a FilePath or AssetObject ID. Minimum length 1 characters; Maximum length 256 characters | | Idempotency-Key | String | No | Optional header. Retry the same key and input within 24 hours; see [Idempotent retries](#atomic-create-replay). | **Response fields**: `200`. Success returns an attachment containing file bytes. Errors before delivery use JSON. Response headers: `Content-Disposition`, `X-Download-Record-Id`, `X-Idempotency-Replayed` Request example: The example puts the raw download-candidate key `p40:a2` in the JSON body as `assetKey`, without URL encoding. Use the key returned by your download-candidate list; it is not a FilePath or AssetObject ID. ```bash curl --request POST 'https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse/product-api' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer your_api_key' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{ "service": "downloadProductAsset", "id": 40, "assetKey": "p40:a2" }' \ --output product-asset.bin ```

title: App authentication
description: Authorize third-party applications and manage enterprise API keys.
markdown:
## Overview

Third-party applications can access enterprise Open APIs after an enterprise administrator enables and authorizes the application. Use appId and appSecretKey to manage API keys, then use those keys to call the core APIs.

## Basics

### Base URLs

- **Mainland China**: https://open.musedam.cc/api/apps
- **Overseas**: https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps

### Authentication

Use **HTTP Basic Authentication**:

- Combine appId and appSecretKey as `appId:appSecretKey` and Base64-encode the string.
- Add the HTTP header: `Authorization: Basic [Base64-encoded value]`.
- All application management requests must include this authentication.

**Authentication example:**

Given the following credentials:

- appId: `test_app_123`
- appSecretKey: `s3cr3t_k3y_456`

**Steps:**

1. Combine appId and appSecretKey: `test_app_123:s3cr3t_k3y_456`.
2. Base64-encode the string: `dGVzdF9hcHBfMTIzOnMzY3IzdF9rM3lfNDU2`.
3. Add the authentication header:

   ```text
   Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS
   ```

> **Note**: Request appId and appSecretKey from your MuseDAM account representative.

### Get an API key

**Endpoint**: `/exchange-api-key`

**Method**: POST

**Request body:**

```text
{
    "orgId":185
}
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "expiresAt": "2055-08-19 16:13:25",
        "org": {
            "id": 185,
            "name": "Example team",
            "orgNo": "M000001",
            "orgFeeType": 4
        }
    },
    "traceId": "17555988913681722512"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/exchange-api-key' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "orgId":185
}'
```

---

### Refresh an API key

**Endpoint**: `/refresh-api-key`

**Method**: POST

**Request body:**

```text
{
    "oldApiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY",
        "expiresAt": "2055-08-19 18:22:18"
    },
    "traceId": "17555989381206489704"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/refresh-api-key' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "oldApiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}'
```

---

### Revoke an API key

**Endpoint**: `/revoke-api-key`

**Method**: POST

**Request body:**

```text
{
    "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}
```

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": true,
    "traceId": "17555989381206489704"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request POST 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/revoke-api-key' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
    "apiKey": "YOUR_API_KEY"
}'
```

---

### Query installation status

**Endpoint**: `/get-install-status?orgId=185`

**Method**: GET

**Response**:

```json
{
    "code": 0,
    "message": "OK",
    "result": {
        "appId": "app_4f8c6e9d2b7a",
        "createAt": "2025-08-18 18:53:27",
        "org": {
            "id": 185,
            "name": "Example team",
            "orgNo": "M000001",
            "orgFeeType": 4
        }
    },
    "traceId": "17555989381206489704"
}
```

Request example:

```bash
curl --location --request GET 'https://open.musedam.ai/api/apps/get-install-status?orgId=185' \
--header 'Authorization: Basic YOUR_BASE64_APP_CREDENTIALS' \
```

title: MCP overview
description: Connect AI clients to your asset library through Model Context Protocol.
markdown:
This guide explains how MCP clients such as Cursor, Claude Desktop, and custom clients connect to the MuseDAM production MCP service using **Streamable HTTP**.
MuseDAM MCP can also be used through a Skill. API documentation and downloads:
https://github.com/kang-oy/musedam-open-api.git

---

## Service overview

| Item | Description |
|-|-|
| Protocol | Model Context Protocol (MCP) |
| Capabilities | MuseDAM Open APIs exposed as MCP tools: asset search, upload, editing, tags, folders, shared link search, team information, and more |
| Authentication | A MuseDAM API key is required. See the API guide to obtain an `api_key` |

### Production endpoint and regions

| Environment | URL | Description |
|-|-|-|
| Production | `https://mcp-service.musedam.cc` | Defaults to Mainland China (`cn`); append `?region=overseas` for overseas accounts |

---

## Choose a connection method

Connect to the remote MCP service using Streamable HTTP, without deploying a local process:

| Method | Use case | API key delivery |
|-|-|-|
| **Streamable HTTP** | Client connects to a remote MCP service over HTTP | HTTP `Authorization` header, such as `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` |

---

title: Connect MCP
description: Configure production MCP connections using Streamable HTTP.
markdown:
## Streamable HTTP

### How it works

- The MCP server runs as an HTTP service and supports concurrent clients.
- Clients communicate using standard HTTP requests and JSON-RPC.
- Suitable for remote deployment and multiple clients, such as Cursor URL connections or custom web clients.

### Endpoint and authentication

- **Path**: `/` (root)
- **Method**: `POST` (JSON-RPC requests)
- **Authentication**: Include the API key in the HTTP `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_MUSEDAM_API_KEY>`
- **Region**: Set the optional URL query parameter `?region=<region>`; defaults to `cn`.

### Production connection settings

**Production:**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "musedam": {
      "url": "https://mcp-service.musedam.cc?region=overseas",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_MUSEDAM_API_KEY"
      },
      "name": "MuseDAM"
    }
  }
}
```

Mainland China defaults to `cn` and requires no query parameter. For overseas accounts, use `?region=overseas`, as shown in the English example.

### Configuration parameters

- **url**: Server address. Set the region with `?region=xxx` (optional; defaults to `cn`).

  - Values: `cn` (Mainland China, default), `overseas` (Overseas).
- **headers.Authorization**: Required authentication in `Bearer <api_key>` format.

Some clients use `serverUrl` instead of `url`. Follow your client's configuration format.

### Health check

The service provides a health check endpoint for operations and load balancer probes:

- **Path**: `GET /health_check`
- **Success**: HTTP 200; no response body is required.

Example:

- Production: `https://mcp-service.musedam.cc/health_check`

---

## Regions and APIs

| region | Description | MuseDAM Open API Base URL |
|-|-|-|
| `cn` | Mainland China (default) | `https://open.musedam.cc/api/muse` |
| `overseas` | Overseas | `https://open.musedam.ai/api/muse` |

These MCP tools access MuseDAM through the Open API. HTTP methods follow the corresponding API endpoints, using `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>`. For MCP, configure the key and region through connection settings.

---

## Tool catalog

The following tools follow MCP Tool definitions. Retrieve the current parameter schemas through MCP, or view tool descriptions and parameters in a client such as Cursor.

| Tool | Description |
|-|-|
| `musedam_search_assets` | Search workspace assets by folder, type, keyword, tags, dimensions, and more |
| `musedam_upload_assets` | Upload assets to DAM from downloadable URLs |
| `musedam_modify_assets` | Update asset names, descriptions, ratings, links, and tags |
| `musedam_assets_by_ids` | Get asset details by ID |
| `musedam_folder_subscribe` | Subscribe to or unsubscribe from folder content callbacks |
| `musedam_search_share` | Search assets and folders in a shared link |
| `musedam_merge_tags` | Merge, create, update, or delete enterprise tags in bulk |
| `musedam_set_assets_tags` | Set tags on assets in bulk |
| `musedam_query_tag_tree` | Get the enterprise tag tree |
| `musedam_folder_path` | Get the full path of a folder |
| `musedam_get_sub_folder_ids` | Get all child folder IDs |
| `musedam_get_asset_analysis_result` | Get AI analysis results for an asset |
| `musedam_org_info` | Get team information |
| `musedam_org_member_info` | Get team member information |

---

## Calling conventions

Use MCP `tools/list` to retrieve current parameter schemas, then call tools through `tools/call`. Configure the API key and region in connection settings, not individual tool arguments. Key permissions still apply.
